1.sahih_international: I swear by the Day of Resurrection
1.pickthall: Nay, I swear by the Day of Resurrection;
1.yusuf_ali: I do call to witness the Resurrection Day;
1.shakir: Nay! I swear by the day of resurrection.
1.muhammad_sarwar: I swear by the Day of Resurrection
1.mohsin_khan: I swear by the Day of Resurrection;
1.arberry: No! I swear by the Day of Resurrection.

2.sahih_international: And I swear by the reproaching soul [to the certainty of resurrection].
2.pickthall: Nay, I swear by the accusing soul (that this Scripture is true).
2.yusuf_ali: And I do call to witness the self-reproaching spirit: (Eschew Evil).
2.shakir: Nay! I swear by the self-accusing soul.
2.muhammad_sarwar: and by the self accusing soul (that you will certainly be resurrected).
2.mohsin_khan: And I swear by the self-reproaching person (a believer).
2.arberry: No! I swear by the reproachful soul.

3.sahih_international: Does man think that We will not assemble his bones?
3.pickthall: Thinketh man that We shall not assemble his bones?
3.yusuf_ali: Does man think that We cannot assemble his bones?
3.shakir: Does man think that We shall not gather his bones?
3.muhammad_sarwar: Do men think that We shall never be able to assemble their bones?
3.mohsin_khan: Does man (a disbeliever) think that We shall not assemble his bones?
3.arberry: What, does man reckon We shall not gather his bones?

4.sahih_international: Yes. [We are] Able [even] to proportion his fingertips.
4.pickthall: Yea, verily. We are Able to restore his very fingers!
4.yusuf_ali: Nay, We are able to put together in perfect order the very tips of his fingers.
4.shakir: Yea! We are able to make complete his very fingertips
4.muhammad_sarwar: We certainly have the power to restore them even the very tips of their finger.
4.mohsin_khan: Yes, We are Able to put together in perfect order the tips of his fingers.
4.arberry: Yes indeed; We are able to shape again his fingers.

5.sahih_international: But man desires to continue in sin.
5.pickthall: But man would fain deny what is before him.
5.yusuf_ali: But man wishes to do wrong (even) in the time in front of him.
5.shakir: Nay! man desires to give the lie to what is before him.
5.muhammad_sarwar: In fact, people want to have eternal life in this world.
5.mohsin_khan: Nay! (Man denies Resurrection and Reckoning. So) he desires to continue committing sins.
5.arberry: Nay, but man desires to continue on as a libertine,

6.sahih_international: He asks, "When is the Day of Resurrection?"
6.pickthall: He asketh: When will be this Day of Resurrection?
6.yusuf_ali: He questions: "When is the Day of Resurrection?"
6.shakir: He asks: When is the day of resurrection?
6.muhammad_sarwar: He asks, "When will be the Day of Judgment?"
6.mohsin_khan: He asks: "When will be this Day of Resurrection?"
6.arberry: asking, 'When shall be the Day of Resurrection?'

7.yusuf_ali: At length, when the sight is dazed,
7.shakir: So when the sight becomes dazed,
7.mohsin_khan: So, when the sight shall be dazed,
7.arberry: But when the sight is dazed

8.yusuf_ali: And the moon is buried in darkness.
8.mohsin_khan: And the moon will be eclipsed,

9.sahih_international: And the sun and the moon are joined,
9.pickthall: And sun and moon are united,
9.yusuf_ali: And the sun and moon are joined together,-
9.shakir: And the sun and the moon are brought together,
9.muhammad_sarwar: and the sun and the moon are brought together,
9.mohsin_khan: And the sun and moon will be joined together (by going one into the other or folded up or deprived of their light, etc.)
9.arberry: and the sun and moon are brought together,

10.sahih_international: Man will say on that Day, "Where is the [place of] escape?"
10.pickthall: On that day man will cry: Whither to flee!
10.yusuf_ali: That Day will Man say: "Where is the refuge?"
10.shakir: Man shall say on that day: Whither to fly to?
10.muhammad_sarwar: people will say, "Is there anywhere to run away?"
10.mohsin_khan: On that Day man will say: "Where (is the refuge) to flee?"
10.arberry: upon that day man shall say, 'Whither to flee?'

11.yusuf_ali: By no means! No place of safety!
11.shakir: By no means! there shall be no place of refuge!
11.muhammad_sarwar: Certainly not! There will be no place of refuge.

12.sahih_international: To your Lord, that Day, is the [place of] permanence.
12.pickthall: Unto thy Lord is the recourse that day.
12.yusuf_ali: Before thy Lord (alone), that Day will be the place of rest.
12.shakir: With your Lord alone shall on that day be the place of rest.
12.muhammad_sarwar: The only place of refuge will be with God.
12.mohsin_khan: Unto your Lord (Alone) will be the place of rest that Day.
12.arberry: Upon that day the recourse shall be to thy Lord.

13.sahih_international: Man will be informed that Day of what he sent ahead and kept back.
13.pickthall: On that day man is told the tale of that which he hath sent before and left behind.
13.yusuf_ali: That Day will Man be told (all) that he put forward, and all that he put back.
13.shakir: Man shall on that day be informed of what he sent before and (what he) put off.
13.muhammad_sarwar: On that day, people will be informed of all that they had done and all that they were supposed to do.
13.mohsin_khan: On that Day man will be informed of what he sent forward (of his evil or good deeds), and what he left behind (of his good or evil traditions).
13.arberry: Upon that day man shall be told his former deeds and his latter;

14.sahih_international: Rather, man, against himself, will be a witness,
14.pickthall: Oh, but man is a telling witness against himself,
14.yusuf_ali: Nay, man will be evidence against himself,
14.shakir: Nay! man is evidence against himself,
14.muhammad_sarwar: In fact, people are well-aware of their own soul
14.mohsin_khan: Nay! Man will be a witness against himself [as his body parts (skin, hands, legs, etc.) will speak about his deeds].
14.arberry: nay, man shall be a clear proof against himself,

15.sahih_international: Even if he presents his excuses.
15.yusuf_ali: Even though he were to put up his excuses.
15.shakir: Though he puts forth his excuses.
15.mohsin_khan: Though he may put forth his excuses (to cover his evil deeds).
15.arberry: even though he offer his excuses.

16.sahih_international: Move not your tongue with it, [O Muhammad], to hasten with recitation of the Qur'an.
16.pickthall: Stir not thy tongue herewith to hasten it.
16.yusuf_ali: Move not thy tongue concerning the (Qur'an) to make haste therewith.
16.shakir: Do not move your tongue with it to make haste with it,
16.muhammad_sarwar: (Muhammad), do not move your tongue too quickly to recite the Quran.
16.mohsin_khan: Move not your tongue concerning (the Quran, O Muhammad SAW) to make haste therewith.
16.arberry: Move not thy tongue with it to hasten it;

17.sahih_international: Indeed, upon Us is its collection [in your heart] and [to make possible] its recitation.
17.pickthall: Lo! upon Us (resteth) the putting together thereof and the reading thereof.
17.yusuf_ali: It is for Us to collect it and to promulgate it:
17.shakir: Surely on Us (devolves) the collecting of it and the reciting of it.
17.muhammad_sarwar: We shall be responsible for its collection and its recitation.
17.mohsin_khan: It is for Us to collect it and to give you (O Muhammad SAW) the ability to recite it (the Quran),
17.arberry: Ours it is to gather it, and to recite it.

18.sahih_international: So when We have recited it [through Gabriel], then follow its recitation.
18.pickthall: And when We read it, follow thou the reading;
18.yusuf_ali: But when We have promulgated it, follow thou its recital (as promulgated):
18.shakir: Therefore when We have recited it, follow its recitation.
18.muhammad_sarwar: When We recite it, follow its recitation (by Us).
18.mohsin_khan: And when We have recited it to you [O Muhammad SAW through Jibrael (Gabriel)], then follow you its (the Quran's) recital.
18.arberry: So, when We recite it, follow thou its recitation.

19.sahih_international: Then upon Us is its clarification [to you].
19.pickthall: Then lo! upon Us (resteth) the explanation thereof.
19.yusuf_ali: Nay more, it is for Us to explain it (and make it clear):
19.shakir: Again on Us (devolves) the explaining of it.
19.muhammad_sarwar: We shall be responsible for its explanation.
19.mohsin_khan: Then it is for Us (Allah) to make it clear to you,
19.arberry: Then Ours it is to explain it.

20.sahih_international: No! But you love the immediate
20.pickthall: Nay, but ye do love the fleeting Now
20.yusuf_ali: Nay, (ye men!) but ye love the fleeting life,
20.shakir: Nay! But you love the present life,
20.muhammad_sarwar: Human beings certainly do not want to pay much attention to the Quran. In fact, they love the worldly life
20.mohsin_khan: Not [as you think, that you (mankind) will not be resurrected and recompensed for your deeds], but (you men) love the present life of this world,
20.arberry: No indeed; but you love the hasty world,

21.muhammad_sarwar: and neglect the life to come.

22.sahih_international: [Some] faces, that Day, will be radiant,
22.pickthall: That day will faces be resplendent,
22.yusuf_ali: Some faces, that Day, will beam (in brightness and beauty);-
22.shakir: (Some) faces on that day shall be bright,
22.muhammad_sarwar: On the Day of Judgment some faces will be bright,
22.mohsin_khan: Some faces that Day shall be Nadirah (shining and radiant).
22.arberry: Upon that day faces shall be radiant,

23.muhammad_sarwar: and look forward to receiving mercy from their Lord.

24.sahih_international: And [some] faces, that Day, will be contorted,
24.pickthall: And that day will other faces be despondent,
24.yusuf_ali: And some faces, that Day, will be sad and dismal,
24.shakir: And (other) faces on that day shall be gloomy,
24.mohsin_khan: And some faces, that Day, will be Basirah (dark, gloomy, frowning, and sad),
24.arberry: and upon that day faces shall be scowling,

25.sahih_international: Expecting that there will be done to them [something] backbreaking.
25.pickthall: Thou wilt know that some great disaster is about to fall on them.
25.yusuf_ali: In the thought that some back-breaking calamity was about to be inflicted on them;
25.shakir: Knowing that there will be made to befall them some great calamity.
25.muhammad_sarwar: certain of facing a great calamity.
25.mohsin_khan: Thinking that some calamity was about to fall on them;
25.arberry: thou mightest think the Calamity has been wreaked on them.

26.sahih_international: No! When the soul has reached the collar bones
26.pickthall: Nay, but when the life cometh up to the throat
26.yusuf_ali: Yea, when (the soul) reaches to the collar-bone (in its exit),
26.shakir: Nay! When it comes up to the throat,
26.muhammad_sarwar: Some people, certainly, do not believe in it, but when a person's soul reaches up to his throat
26.mohsin_khan: Nay, when (the soul) reaches to the collar bone (i.e. up to the throat in its exit),
26.arberry: No indeed; when it reaches the clavicles

27.sahih_international: And it is said, "Who will cure [him]?"
27.pickthall: And men say: Where is the wizard (who can save him now)?
27.yusuf_ali: And there will be a cry, "Who is a magician (to restore him)?"
27.shakir: And it is said: Who will be a magician?
27.muhammad_sarwar: and the angels say, "Who will take away his soul,
27.mohsin_khan: And it will be said: "Who can cure him and save him from death?"
27.arberry: and it is said, 'Who is an enchanter?'

28.sahih_international: And the dying one is certain that it is the [time of] separation
28.pickthall: And he knoweth that it is the parting;
28.yusuf_ali: And he will conclude that it was (the Time) of Parting;
28.shakir: And he is sure that it is the (hour of) parting
28.muhammad_sarwar: (the angels of mercy or the angels of wrath,)" then, he will realize that it is time to leave this world.
28.mohsin_khan: And he (the dying person) will conclude that it was (the time) of departing (death);
28.arberry: and he thinks that it is the parting

29.sahih_international: And the leg is wound about the leg,
29.pickthall: And agony is heaped on agony;
29.yusuf_ali: And one leg will be joined with another:
29.shakir: And affliction is combined with affliction;
29.muhammad_sarwar: When legs are twisted around each other,
29.mohsin_khan: And leg will be joined with another leg (shrouded)
29.arberry: and leg is intertwined with leg,

30.sahih_international: To your Lord, that Day, will be the procession.
30.pickthall: Unto thy Lord that day will be the driving.
30.yusuf_ali: That Day the Drive will be (all) to thy Lord!
30.shakir: To your Lord on that day shall be the driving.
30.muhammad_sarwar: that will be the time to be driven to one's Lord.
30.mohsin_khan: The drive will be, on that Day, to your Lord (Allah)!
30.arberry: upon that day unto thy Lord shall be the driving.

31.sahih_international: And the disbeliever had not believed, nor had he prayed.
31.pickthall: For he neither trusted, nor prayed.
31.yusuf_ali: So he gave nothing in charity, nor did he pray!-
31.shakir: So he did not accept the truth, nor did he pray,
31.muhammad_sarwar: The human being does not want to believe the Truth, nor does he want to pray.
31.mohsin_khan: So he (the disbeliever) neither believed (in this Quran, in the Message of Muhammad SAW) nor prayed!
31.arberry: For he confirmed it not, and did not pray,

32.sahih_international: But [instead], he denied and turned away.
32.yusuf_ali: But on the contrary, he rejected Truth and turned away!
32.shakir: But called the truth a lie and turned back,
32.muhammad_sarwar: He rejects the faith, turns away
32.mohsin_khan: But on the contrary, he belied (this Quran and the Message of Muhammad SAW) and turned away!
32.arberry: but he cried it lies, and he turned away,

33.sahih_international: And then he went to his people, swaggering [in pride].
33.pickthall: Then went he to his folk with glee.
33.yusuf_ali: Then did he stalk to his family in full conceit!
33.shakir: Then he went to his followers, walking away in haughtiness.
33.muhammad_sarwar: and haughtily goes to his people.
33.mohsin_khan: Then he walked in full pride to his family admiring himself!
33.arberry: then he went to his household arrogantly.

34.yusuf_ali: Woe to thee, (O men!), yea, woe!
34.shakir: Nearer to you (is destruction) and nearer,
34.mohsin_khan: Woe to you [O man (disbeliever)]! And then (again) woe to you!

35.sahih_international: Then woe to you, and woe!
35.pickthall: Again nearer unto thee and nearer (is the doom).
35.yusuf_ali: Again, Woe to thee, (O men!), yea, woe!
35.shakir: Again (consider how) nearer to you and nearer.
35.mohsin_khan: Again, woe to you [O man (disbeliever)]! And then (again) woe to you!
35.arberry: then nearer to thee and nearer!

36.sahih_international: Does man think that he will be left neglected?
36.pickthall: Thinketh man that he is to be left aimless?
36.yusuf_ali: Does man think that he will be left uncontrolled, (without purpose)?
36.shakir: Does man think that he is to be left to wander without an aim?
36.muhammad_sarwar: For you, the human being of such behavior, will certainly deserve it.
36.mohsin_khan: Does man think that he will be left Suda [neglected without being punished or rewarded for the obligatory duties enjoined by his Lord (Allah) on him]?
36.arberry: What, does man reckon he shall be left to roam at will?

37.sahih_international: Had he not been a sperm from semen emitted?
37.pickthall: Was he not a drop of fluid which gushed forth?
37.yusuf_ali: Was he not a drop of sperm emitted (in lowly form)?
37.shakir: Was he not a small seed in the seminal elements,
37.muhammad_sarwar: Does the human being think that he will be left uncontrolled?
37.mohsin_khan: Was he not a Nutfah (mixed male and female discharge of semen) poured forth?
37.arberry: Was he not a sperm-drop spilled?

38.sahih_international: Then he was a clinging clot, and [Allah] created [his form] and proportioned [him]
38.pickthall: Then he became a clot; then (Allah) shaped and fashioned
38.yusuf_ali: Then did he become a leech-like clot; then did (Allah) make and fashion (him) in due proportion.
38.shakir: Then he was a clot of blood, so He created (him) then made (him) perfect.
38.muhammad_sarwar: Was he not once just a drop of discharged sperm.
38.mohsin_khan: Then he became an 'Alaqa (a clot); then (Allah) shaped and fashioned (him) in due proportion.
38.arberry: Then he was a blood-clot, and He created and formed,

39.sahih_international: And made of him two mates, the male and the female.
39.pickthall: And made of him a pair, the male and female.
39.yusuf_ali: And of him He made two sexes, male and female.
39.shakir: Then He made of him two kinds, the male and the female.
39.muhammad_sarwar: Was he not turned into a clot of blood? God then formed him and gave him proper shape. From the human being, God made males and females in pairs.
39.mohsin_khan: And made him in two sexes, male and female.
39.arberry: and He made of him two kinds, male and female.

40.sahih_international: Is not that [Creator] Able to give life to the dead?
40.pickthall: Is not He (Who doeth so) Able to bring the dead to life?
40.yusuf_ali: Has not He, (the same), the power to give life to the dead?
40.shakir: Is not He able to give life to the dead?
40.muhammad_sarwar: Does He then not have the power to bring the dead back to life?
40.mohsin_khan: Is not He (Allah Who does that), Able to give life to the dead? (Yes! He is Able to do all things).
40.arberry: What, is He not able to quicken the dead?
